item.title: Track Catalogue 0.9.2
item.description:
• Faster with large catalogues. With thousands of songs, a new set opens, generates and answers clicks much sooner, and saving writes only what changed: opening the catalogue no longer writes every song again. While a set reads its songs or generates, you can see that the app is busy.
  • Song details keep your changes. After Undo, or a part dragged on the chart, while the cursor was in a field such as Use until, leaving the field no longer puts the old value back.
  • On Windows, a set's length stays as you typed it when you change its curve, and an open set follows changes to its songs in the catalogue.

item.title: Track Catalogue 0.9.1
item.description:
• Songs cut to follow the curve. Generate may now end a song early, or start it later, where its music changes and the curve has moved away from it, and it may leave out intros and outros. A cut song's details say what plays, and Play Uncut plays it whole again. It's on in new sets and off in sets you saved before; switch it in the set's options.
  • Loops. Mark a part of a song to repeat with Loop Part… in its details, under Leave Out Parts. Hear the Join plays the crossfade back to the part's start. Generate may then repeat the part to play the song longer, up to the number of times you set. In a set, drag a song's end to add or remove whole repeats, or use Repeat Its Loop Once More in its menu. The song stays as it is in the catalogue and in other sets.
  • Smoother big imports. While songs are analysed, the app saves only what changed, once per song and in the background, so the catalogue no longer stalls. A song still being analysed when you quit is analysed again at the next start.

item.title: Track Catalogue 0.9
item.description:
• Hear only the vocals, or only the music. Under Play in a song's details: Both, Vocals or Music. Switching separates the song in a few seconds, on your computer, and it plays on from the same place. Use it to check whether a song has vocals, or whether its words can be understood. The first time, the app asks to download a model (80 MB); Settings can remove it. It's only for listening: sets are unchanged. Not on Intel Macs.
  • Transitions remembered across sets. The last transition you set between two songs (its kind, length, beat offset, fade shape or drawn fades) comes back whenever the same two songs meet in a set for the first time: in a new set, or after Generate. Sets you've prepared keep the transitions they have. The first start after the update learns them from the sets you've saved.
  • When the pool runs short of an intensity. An orange band under the curve says which intensity is missing and about how many more songs it needs. Generate asks first: approximate with the nearest intensities, or add the catalogue's songs at that intensity to the pool. Songs standing in are marked, such as "7 for 9".
  • Copy to Catalogue. Right-click selected songs to copy them to another catalogue, or to a new one, with everything you've set and everything the analysis found.
  • Nothing is sent to Microsoft. The library that finds vocals and separates songs no longer reports its use.

item.title: Track Catalogue 0.8.2
item.description:
• Check for Updates in About. About Track Catalogue now has a Check for Updates button, so you can look for a new version from there too.
  • Words names the language. The catalogue's Words column says which language it found, such as "Understood (English)" or "Not Understood (Irish)", so you can check it at a glance.

item.title: Track Catalogue 0.8.1
item.description:
• Big collections analyse at an even pace. The catalogues now live in the app's song database instead of one big file that was written again after every change. With thousands of songs, analysis no longer slows down as the catalogue grows. On the first start, your catalogues move in by themselves; the old files are kept as backups.
  • Windows keeps its settings. Windows forgot every setting at each start: window sizes, Settings, the chart layers. It keeps them now, and What's New shows only once after an update.

item.title: Track Catalogue 0.8
item.description:
• Vocals found by listening. The analysis now finds where songs have singing or speech, and fills in Vocals by itself (None, Some, Throughout). Songs without vocals aren't looked up online any more. The first start after the update reads every song once more, in the background.
  • A song's language, heard on your computer. Where MusicBrainz doesn't know the language, the app offers once to download a language model (140 MB) and listens to each such song's most vocal 30 seconds. Nothing is sent. When it can't tell, it says "Unclear", which counts as not understood. Detect Language by Listening in a song's Words menu does it by hand. Settings can remove the model.
  • Layers in every chart. Intensity, Waveform, Vocals and, in a set, Volume: switch each on and off with the small buttons next to a chart, with ⌥1 to ⌥4 (Alt+1 to Alt+4 on Windows), or in the View menu. ⌥0 shows them all. Vocals shades where the singing is, so you can listen in quickly.
  • Drawn fades. In a transition's details, choose Fade › Drawn and shape each song's volume with points: click a line to add one, drag it, double-click to remove it, and drag the small handle between two points to bend that stretch. Reset to Shape goes back. For a bass swap, EQ blend or filter sweep, draw its volume with Draw (Draw Volume at the top right of the close-up on Windows).
  • The set's volume line. Switch on the Volume layer, click the line across the timeline to add a point, and drag it up or down to make that part of the set louder or quieter. Reset Volume in the set's options takes it away.
  • How much keys count. A set's options have Keys: Off, Some (as before), Strong, or Must Fit, where songs whose keys clash never follow each other.
  • The details scroll on. Under the timeline, scroll sideways from song to transition to song (on Windows, also with the bar under them). While the set plays, they follow what plays; Follow brings that back after you've scrolled away.

item.title: Track Catalogue 0.7
item.description:
• Vocals and words. Songs have two new values, Vocals (None, Some, Throughout) and Words (Understood, Not Understood, None), as columns in the catalogue, in a song's details and in its right-click menu. Words comes by itself: the app looks up the language of a song's lyrics on MusicBrainz, sending only its artist and title, and compares it with the languages people understand, which you tick in Settings. What you set yourself always wins. Please check what it found for your songs: hover over Words to see the language.
  • Sets without understood words. In a set's options, Understood Words can be Include, Exclude (no such song anywhere in the set, transitions included) or Per Phase: right-click a phase and choose Leave Out Understood Words, for example for Heart. Prolong and Change the Set keep to it while the set plays.
  • Settings has "Look up song languages online", on unless you switch it off, and the list of understood languages: English and your computer's language to start with.

item.title: Track Catalogue 0.6
item.description:
• Updates from inside the app. Track Catalogue checks for new versions by itself and asks before it installs one: Install, Later or Skip This Version. It never asks while a set plays. After an update, this window shows what's new. You can switch the checks off in Settings, and check by hand with Check for Updates….
  • Fade shapes. Crossfades fade in one of four shapes, Even, Smooth, Slow Out or Slow In, picked by the music unless you choose one for the set or a transition. A set can end with a fade to silence.
  • Leaving out parts of a song. Leave Out Parts… in a song's details marks stretches to skip, such as a long spoken intro. Sets play the song without them, with short crossfades at the joins. Save as New Song… keeps the original as it was, and can write the shorter version as its own file.
  • A song's level by ear. A Level slider in a song's details makes it louder or quieter than levelled, in every set. The catalogue's preview plays levelled now, like a set.
  • Folders opened with the app, or dropped on its icon, are added to the catalogue, like Add Folder.
  • Windows: Go Live is a red button, the pool in the set window can be made wider, and a crash is fixed that could happen when a changed transition played past the end of a song from a CD.
